matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, its orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) must stay unchanged; you cannot rotate a stick to a different orientation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you relocate a stick, check that its orientation remains the same.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick and rotating it to become vertical, producing an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick must be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After deciding which stick to move, ensure the total stick count stays constant.
matchstick.example: Adding an extra horizontal stick to turn '+' into '×' without removing any stick elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After the move, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a permitted operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after repositioning the stick, verify each character matches a known symbol.
matchstick.example: Leaving a single diagonal after removing one from an X, which is not a recognized numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of the left and right sides of the transformed equation and confirm they are equal before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After constructing a candidate equation, perform the arithmetic check.
matchstick.example: Accepting a visually correct arrangement like 'XV = XIII + IV' without confirming that 15 = 13 + 4.

matchstick.title: Operator swap via stick exchange
matchstick.principle: You may move a stick from one operator to another, changing both operators, provided the resulting symbols are valid operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic discrepancy suggests changing '+' to '-' or similar, consider moving a stick between operators.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to '=' and ending up with two '-' signs and no '=' sign.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: Never leave an X or V with only one diagonal after moving a stick; the remaining single diagonal does not form a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before moving a diagonal from an X or V, ensure you will reposition it within the same numeral or that the source numeral will stay valid.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an X, leaving a lone diagonal that is not a Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Cross‑numeral stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved from one numeral to another, but both the source and destination must remain valid Roman numerals after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single‑stick move between different numerals could adjust values, verify both numerals stay legal.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V to an I, leaving the V with a single diagonal (invalid) and the I unchanged.

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved to a different location within the same numeral, changing its shape (e.g., V ↔ X) as long as the resulting numeral is valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic discrepancy is small (often 5), try repositioning a diagonal inside a V or X rather than moving it between characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V to a new crossing position within the same V but forgetting to complete the crossing, leaving an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Equality sign preservation
matchstick.principle: The equation must contain exactly one '=' sign after the move; you cannot turn it into another operator or remove it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick relocation, check that the '=' sign still consists of two horizontal sticks.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal line from '=', turning it into a '-' and leaving no equality sign.

matchstick.title: Value‑adjusting V↔X transformation
matchstick.principle: If the numeric difference between the two sides is exactly 5 (or a multiple thereof), consider converting a V to an X or an X to a V within the same numeral; this changes the value by 5 while preserving stick count.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the arithmetic discrepancy, if it equals 5 (or 10, 15, …), look for a V↔X change via within‑numeral repositioning.
matchstick.example: Changing a V to an X to increase a side by 5 but forgetting to keep the original V valid, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making symbols valid and may assume visual correctness implies arithmetic correctness.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides after any transformation and confirm equality before finalizing.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving sticks between operators, the model may unintentionally create or destroy an operator symbol, violating the single‑equals requirement.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving sticks, explicitly count the operators; ensure there is exactly one '=', and any other operators remain as originally allowed.
